prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “official” service that reports what LLMs (ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat, etc.) will recommend, so the best approach is a two‑part strategy: (A) use a local‑listings/knowledge‑graph management service to make sure LLMs have accurate facts about your business, and (B) run regular direct checks against the LLMs themselves (automated where possible).

Recommended services and why

- Yext — Best if you want centralized control of your “knowledge graph” (name, hours, services, attributes). Yext distributes accurate facts to many platforms and positions you to show up in AI-driven answers.
- Uberall / Moz Local / BrightLocal / Whitespark — Good, lower‑cost alternatives for citation/listing distribution and local SEO. BrightLocal and Whitespark are especially useful for local ranking and review monitoring.
- Google Business Profile (free) — must-have. If Google has your facts, many downstream systems and knowledge graphs will too.
- Review/reputation tools (BirdEye, Podium, Trustpilot, Mention/Awario/Brand24) — track reviews and brand mentions; many LLMs rely on reputation signals.
- SEO suites (SEMrush, Ahrefs, Moz) — track organic visibility and queries that could trigger recommendations.

How to check whether LLMs recommend you

1. Direct querying (most reliable)
   - Manually prompt ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat with realistic user queries (“best [service] near [city]”, “who do you recommend for [specific need]?”) and see if your business appears.
   - Automate via APIs where available: use the OpenAI API (GPT‑4/4o) to run a battery of query variations and parse outputs for mentions. For Bard/Bing Chat you may need manual checks or browser automation (respect platform terms).
   - Test many prompt variants, locations, user intents and personas (e.g., price‑sensitive, emergency).

2. Monitor the knowledge sources LLMs use
   - Ensure accurate, consistent NAP (name/address/phone), hours, categories, and structured data (schema.org LocalBusiness) on your site.
   - Be present and optimized on Google Business Profile, Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, and major directories — LLMs often pull from those sources or the knowledge graphs they feed.
   - Claim or create a Wikidata/Wikipedia presence if your business qualifies — many models reference Wikidata.

3. Set up periodic tests
   - Weekly or monthly automated tests via the OpenAI API for a representative list of queries.
   - Log results, track changes, and correlate with changes you make (new reviews, updated listings).

Which single option to pick
- If you want one paid vendor to focus on: Yext is the most explicitly geared toward feeding accurate knowledge into search/AI environments; combine it with periodic API checks of ChatGPT (OpenAI API) to see actual model behavior.
- If you’re on a tight budget: claim and optimize Google Business Profile + use BrightLocal or Moz Local for citations, and run occasional manual ChatGPT/Bard queries.

Quick checklist to improve the chances an LLM will recommend you
- Claim and fully complete Google Business Profile + other major directories.
- Add schema.org LocalBusiness structured data to your site.
- Get steady, high‑quality reviews on Google/Yelp/etc.
- Create clear “service + location” pages and FAQ content that answers common user questions.
- Get listed in authoritative directories and, if possible, Wikidata/Wikipedia entries.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a list of 50 realistic user prompts to test across LLMs.
- Provide a small OpenAI API script to run those prompts and parse results for mentions.
- Recommend the best pick for your budget and industry if you tell me location, industry, and budget.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
